outcome: Hospital mortality/severe brain injury (grade 3/4 intraventricular hemorrhage and/or periventricular leukomalacia)
cohort: The study included 6137 extremely preterm singleton infants <29 weeks' gestation who were admitted to units participating in the Canadian Neonatal Network between January 2015 and December 2022.
finding: Deferred cord clamping after cesarean deliveries was associated with lower odds of a composite of mortality/severe brain injury compared to both deferred cord clamping after vaginal deliveries and early cord clamping after cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Infants who received deferred cord clamping after cesarean deliveries had lower odds of mortality/severe brain injury than those who received deferred cord clamping after vaginal deliveries.
